question: By what means does a speaker claim to have come to know the determination of Kaula?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas.
The speaker claims to have become known or to know through another's grace.
That knowledge is specified as the determination of Kaula.
The agent of that knowledge is the speaker.
inference: By the grace of the lord of Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the determination of Kaula.
uncertainties: Ambiguity between jñāta as known and as knower remains
plain_english: By your grace, O lord of Kaulas, I have come to know the determination of Kaula.
